purpose: This record compares the current native boolean backends across the normal production producer workload.

method.scheduler: The unchanged hsm-print-build scheduler, dependency graph, staging and two active producer slots.
method.sources: Both backends execute the same current recipes, including the same sampling and mold optimizations. Only the hsm-manifold boundary selects the alternate engine.
method.inputs: External inputs are copied from one fixed snapshot. Dependencies consume newly generated outputs from their own backend within each full run.
method.caches: Whole-producer result reuse is bypassed. Enclosure construction caches are disabled. Installed-machine caches start empty in private producer roots. Each backend retains its own STEP import cache between rounds. Content-addressed scene assets share the normal immutable store.
method.publication: Disabled; the scheduler check-current mode suppresses checkout carry and checkpoints while the private adapter deliberately executes producers.
method.scope: Precompiled producer execution and scheduler wall time, including generation, exports and downstream normal documentation. Compilation, native result-store lookup and publication are outside the timed workload.
method.host: The timing lease excludes other scheduler-managed heavy runs. Ordinary desktop services continue.
method.memory_scope: The largest individual producer process RSS is reported, not combined system or concurrent process memory.
method.distribution_threshold: The descriptive material-change counts require both a relative change over ten percent and an absolute change over a tenth of a second; this is not an automatic gate.

source.purpose: This record identifies the pinned Rust boolean source and its local inlining patch.

src/boolean3_kernels.rs.change: Inline the hot exact-intersection helpers into their callers under standard floating-point rules.

rust.patch: Current pinned source with the existing scalar-kernel inlining annotations.

build.purpose: This record identifies the private C++ reference compilation.

validation.production_source_edits: None. The reference manifest and lockfile are restored after the private compile.
validation.limits: This is a production-workload performance comparison. Different mesh hashes across backends do not by themselves establish a geometric deviation; it does not replace a full physical-equivalence audit for a production rollback.

interpretation.earlier_comparison: The earlier samples covered only selected producers and combined recipe changes with the engine change. They do not establish the performance effect of the engine swap.
interpretation.current: The current Rust backend increases latency for this complete fresh producer workload relative to the C++ reference on the same recipes.
interpretation.recommendation: Discuss restoring the C++ native boolean backend for production and evaluate further Rust engine changes against the complete workload.
